Recommended architecture (concise)

- Use the Global Chart of Accounts master as your source-of-truth; create any new accounts there first and then assign only the accounts you will actively use to the Company chart. If you replace an account (e.g. Inventory) you must update the GL defaults that reference it [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_ListGlAccountOrganization.adoc-0].

- Represent each physical outlet as an OFBiz ProductStore (productStoreId). ProductStore already models per‑store warehouses/facilities and scopes orders/fulfillment by store, so it is the natural tenant/scope for per‑store reporting and isolation while keeping a single business database for shared warehouse processes [doc:applications/product/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/product-stores.adoc-2] [430408956-2].

- Profitability per store: keep global GL revenue accounts in the master chart but use the Sales Invoice item-type overrides to map sales revenue to store‑specific (or department‑specific) GL accounts where you need isolated reporting. The Sales Invoice screen supports per-item overrides precisely to isolate sales reporting for a department/business unit [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_GlAccountSalInvoice.adoc-0].

- Cash reconciliation per store: either use store‑specific cash/bank GL accounts assigned from the global chart, or create per‑store receipt/clearing accounts in the global chart and assign them via GL defaults so receipts/payments are posted per store. Remember: new accounts must be linked in GL defaults to take effect [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_ListGlAccountOrganization.adoc-0].

- Internal transfers & centralized procurement: keep Inventory and Cost of Goods accounts in the global chart and ensure GL defaults reference them. For transfers between main warehouse and store warehouses (or store-to-store), post the inventory movement to the inventory/transfer GL accounts you select in the global chart; if you need per‑store inventory valuation, provide store‑specific inventory/transfer accounts and wire them into GL defaults. Always update GL defaults when you change which Inventory account is used [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_ListGlAccountOrganization.adoc-0].

- Taxes: map each tax authority to its own GL account so amounts collected/paid to different authorities are tracked separately (set up under Tax Authority / GL Account defaults) [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_EditOrganizationTaxAuthorityGlAccounts.adoc-0].

Practical steps
1. Review the Global GL master; add any store-specific revenue/cash/inventory/transfer accounts there. Assign only needed accounts to the Company chart. Test GL defaults after adding accounts [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_ListGlAccountOrganization.adoc-0].
2. Configure each outlet as a ProductStore with its warehouses/facilities so transactions carry productStoreId for scoping [doc:applications/product/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/product-stores.adoc-2] [430408956-2].
3. Use Sales Invoice item-type overrides to map store revenue to store GL accounts where required for profitability reporting [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_GlAccountSalInvoice.adoc-0].
4. Map tax authorities to GL accounts to separate tax flows [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_EditOrganizationTaxAuthorityGlAccounts.adoc-0].

Short answer — your steps exposed known demo-data / permissions issues, not a mysterious bug in OFBiz core. Actions to take and why:

What likely went wrong
- You loaded the demo data, which includes the admin party and multiple default userLogin accounts (and weak default passwords). Running with demo data commonly leaves accounts and permissions open enough that other demo users can view/edit things they shouldn’t [7045138-8][7045142-1].  
- OFBiz enforces access by permissions/roles (including role‑limited permissions). If a user/party or group was accidentally given a broad permission or the “admin” permission (or a group containing it), that overrides other checks and allows edits [48202125-0][7045134-12].

Immediate remediation steps
1. Don’t run with demo credentials in production — change or disable all demo/user logins (admin, flexadmin, demoadmin, etc.) using Party Manager: find the party → user names → edit password or disable the login [7045142-1][7045138-8].  
2. Verify and remove any admin/admin-like permission or overly-broad security group assigned to democustomer (use Party Manager to inspect roles/permissions assigned to that userLogin/party). Ensure role-limited permissions are only granted where intended [48202125-0][7045134-12].  
3. If you don’t need the demo dataset, rebuild/load only seed data and create a single admin account instead. Example: load seed-only and create admin via gradle (as docs show) rather than loading full demo: ./gradlew "ofbiz --load-data readers=seed,seed-initial" loadAdminUserLogin -PuserLoginId=admin (or use readers=seed,ext for custom data) [170266058-42][7045138-8].  
4. Check login/disable config (login.disable.minutes) if you disable accounts so they don’t auto‑re-enable unexpectedly [7045142-1].

Why these fixes help
- The docs explicitly warn never to use demo credentials and to change/disable demo accounts, and explain the admin permission semantics (admin permission takes precedence) and how security is assigned via roles/groups/permissions [7045142-1][7045134-12][48202125-0][7045138-8].

- This is caused by the Webtools entity search loading far too much into JVM heap; Webtools provides tools to force GC/clear caches and you should avoid pulling millions of rows into the UI. Use batch/paginated processing (a service that fetches smaller chunks) or import/export tooling instead [doc:webtools-main.adoc-0] [27840504-4] [48201990-5].

Practical steps
1) Immediate recovery: use Webtools → Cache & Debug to clear caches or force Garbage Collection to free memory so the UI becomes responsive again [doc:webtools-main.adoc-0].  
2) Don’t browse millions of rows in the Entity search UI. Instead implement a service (Groovy DSL is available) that uses the entity API (runService/findList etc. use the delegator automatically) and fetches/processes records in smaller batches (pagination) to avoid loading all records into memory [27840504-4].  
3) Add error handling around the service/entity calls (try/catch) if you need special handling instead of the default service rollback behavior [27840504-4].  
4) For large data moves or bulk inspection use Webtools import/export or the install.jsp loading mechanisms (XML/SQL files) rather than the interactive search UI [48201990-5] [184617942-12].

Short answer / recommended approach
- Use OFBiz’s built-in multitenancy: identify tenant either by tenant ID (login form) or by tenant-specific URL/domain, and route requests so OFBiz selects the tenant’s datasource at request time [14814279-1][49579254-1][49579254-2].
- Keep tenant data isolated with one database per tenant (configure per-tenant datasources in yourTenantConfig.xml). Use the default database only for shared/system data [14814279-1][14814279-4].
- For the frontend, host the React app in a multitenant-aware way (tenant-specific domains or host-based routing). Ensure each API call carries the tenant context (host → tenant mapping or an explicit tenantId) so OFBiz can select the proper tenant DB and configuration [49579254-2][49579254-1].

Practical steps
1. Configure tenants in OFBiz:
   - Add <Tenant> entries and corresponding <TenantDataSource> entries (tenantId, jdbcUri, credentials) in yourTenantConfig.xml so OFBiz points to each tenant DB [14814279-4].
2. Frontend routing / tenant discovery:
   - Use tenant-specific domains or tenant-aware URLs so the React app and API gateway can determine the tenant for each request (OFBiz supports front-store multitenancy and tenant-specific domains) [49579254-2][49579254-1].
3. Authentication:
   - Have users authenticate against the tenant they are accessing (login with tenantId or via tenant URL); let OFBiz establish the tenant-scoped session/server context based on that tenant selection [14814279-1][49579254-1].
4. Tenant-specific configuration:
   - Store tenant-specific configuration attributes so the backend behavior and UI can be customized per tenant (multitenancy extensions include tenant-specific configuration support) [49579254-1].

When to avoid per-merchant DBs
- If you need multiple merchants to share facilities/stock/etc., consider a merchant-account model (e.g., ProductStore scoping) rather than per-merchant databases — per-merchant DBs can fragment shared operations; the fulfillment design discussion recommends ProductStore-based scoping for multi-merchant within shared operations [430408956-2].

- OFBiz multitenancy is implemented as one DB per tenant by default; a default DB still exists for shared data [14814279-1].
- Frontend multitenancy (tenant-specific domains, multi-site) is supported so you can run a React front end per-tenant domain or map hosts to tenants [49579254-2][49579254-1].

Short answer: there is no special “automatic” SUP_RETURN_COMPLETED ECA unless one was added for the supplier/purchase-return service in your instance. ECAs run per service/event, so to generate the purchase-return (debit note) you must add an ECA that fires when the purchase-return service commits with status SUP_RETURN_COMPLETED and call the invoice/debit-note creation service.

What to do (concise steps)
- Identify the service used to change the purchase-return header (the supplier/purchase-return equivalent of updateReturnHeader). ECAs are bound to a specific service and event [7045171-16].  
- Add a service-eca entry for that service with event="commit" and conditions like:
  - statusId equals SUP_RETURN_COMPLETED
  - oldStatusId not-equals SUP_RETURN_COMPLETED
- Add an <action> that invokes your debit-note / purchase-invoice creation service (mode sync/async as needed). Use <set> to map any parameters the action service needs into the service context before calling it [7045171-16].
- Place the new <service-eca> xml in the appropriate component/service definition file and test.

Example ECA (template)
<service-eca>
  <eca service="updateReturnHeader" event="commit">
    <condition field-name="statusId" operator="equals" value="SUP_RETURN_COMPLETED"/>
    <condition field-name="oldStatusId" operator="not-equals" value="SUP_RETURN_COMPLETED"/>
    <!-- use <set> to map parameters as needed -->
    <action service="yourCreatePurchaseReturnInvoiceService" mode="sync"/>
  </eca>
</service-eca>

Notes
- ECAs are evaluated for each service/event and each condition must be true before actions run — so there is nothing implicit that creates a purchase-return invoice unless an ECA/action exists for that service and status change [7045171-16].  
- The returns flow in the Order application shows returns and status-driven steps; implement the analogous ECA for the supplier/purchase-return flow to trigger invoice/debit-note creation at SUP_RETURN_COMPLETED [doc:applications/order/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/order-return.adoc-0].

References: ECA definition, syntax and <set> tip; Returns overview [7045171-16] [doc:applications/order/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/order-return.adoc-0].

Short answer: OFBiz’s scheduler already stores jobs in DB (JobSandbox/RuntimeData) and each node runs a poller thread that looks at the DB — so you can reduce detection/recovery latency by tuning the scheduler/poller thread settings. If you need true “lease + heartbeat” ownership semantics you’ll need to propose/implement an entity/code change (add lease timestamps and ownership-recovery logic) via the project roadmap/JIRA process.

Key facts from the docs
- Jobs are persisted (JobSandbox and RuntimeData), and scheduled jobs are managed by the scheduler, not XML files [7045171-7].
- The scheduler is multi-threaded, has a single poller thread and separate invoker threads; there is one Job Scheduler per ServiceDispatcher/GenericDelegator [7045171-7].
- Polling is configurable: poll-enabled and poll-db-millis control whether and how often the poller thread checks the database. Thread-pool attributes (ttl, wait-millis, jobs, min/max-threads) control invoker thread behavior [48201960-3].

Practical, doc-backed steps you can take now
- Ensure poll-enabled=true and reduce poll-db-millis so the poller runs more frequently (reduces time until another node sees a job) [48201960-3].
- Tune thread-pool attributes (wait-millis, jobs, ttl, min/max-threads) so invoker threads are created and recycled in a way that fits your load and shortens recovery time for re-queued work [48201960-3].
- Confirm all nodes share the same GenericDelegator/DB (so the JobSandbox/RuntimeData are visible across nodes), because there is one scheduler per GenericDelegator [7045171-7].

When to change code / file a JIRA
- The lease+heartbeat approach you outlined (add leaseUpdatedStamp, periodic renewals, expiry-based recovery) requires changing entities and scheduler logic (not covered by the existing docs). Submit a roadmap/JIRA proposal so the change can be reviewed and implemented in OFBiz following the project process [6553737-0].

References: Job storage and scheduler behavior [7045171-7]; scheduler poll/thread-pool configuration options [48201960-3]; roadmap/JIRA process for proposing changes [6553737-0].
